newsitem.title: USA: Lilly's Prozac cleared by FDA for bulimia.
newsitem.headline: Lilly's Prozac cleared by FDA for bulimia.

text.p: Eli Lilly and Co said Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared Prozac to be marketed for the treatment of bulimia nervosa, an eating disorder.
Lilly said this marks the third marketing approval for Prozac, which has been previously cleared by the FDA for use in the treatment of clinical depression and obsessive-compulsive disorder.

Lilly said Prozac, an antidepressant, is the first medicine in the United States to be cleared for marketing by the FDA to treat bulimia nervosa, an eating disorder that afflicts more than one million Americans each year.

Bulimia is an illness characterized by recurrent episodes of uncontrolled binge-eating followed by some type of compensatory behavior, most often purging, which includes self-induced vomiting or misuse of laxatives and diuretics. The disorder strikes women almost exclusively.

Clinical studies have demonstrated that treatment with Prozac leads to a significant reduction in binge-eating and purging episodes, Freda Lewis-Hall, director of the Lilly Center for Women's Health, said.
The most common side effects reported in the bulimia clinical trials included insomnia, nausea, anxiety and asthenia, which is the loss of strength, Lilly said.

Prozac is the most widely prescribed branded antidepressant in the world, Lilly said. It was cleared for marketing in the United States for the treatment of clinical depression in 1987 and for obsessive-compulsive disorder in 1994.
Lilly said it is estimated that more than 24 million people worldwide, including more than 18 million people in the United States, have been treated with Prozac since its introduction.

To date, Prozac has been made available for use in the treatment of depression in 107 countries and for obsessive-compulsive disorder in 39 countries. The United States is the 34th country in which Prozac has received an indication for the treatment of bulimia.
